lines.t: Did you end up going to the career fair?

options: It ends at four this afternoon.
I'm hoping for a career in finance.
No, I didn't know you were going.
I did, and I actually got two interviews out of it.
optionNotes: Repeats 'career' but doesn't say whether the speaker went.
Talks about the other person going, not about oneself.
Correct: says yes and adds a result.
questions.explanation: 'Did you end up going' means 'did you finally go'. D answers yes and adds a natural detail. A confuses 'end up' with an ending time.

lines.t: I'd go with the cheaper laptop if I were you.

options: If I were you, I'd go too.
Yeah, but the cheaper one only has half the memory.
I left my laptop in the library.
I went there yesterday with my sister.
optionNotes: Correct: responds to the advice with a reasonable objection.
questions.explanation: 'Go with' means 'choose'. The speaker is giving advice; B reacts to it with a counter-argument, which is a natural reply. A and D misread 'go'.

lines.t: Who's teaching the intro to psychology class this semester?

options: It meets on Mondays and Wednesdays.
Doctor Okafor, I think. Same as last year.
I'm teaching myself Spanish.
Psychology is my favorite subject.
optionNotes: Repeats 'teaching' but is about the speaker.
Repeats 'psychology' but doesn't name a teacher.
questions.explanation: 'Who' needs a person. B names the instructor. A is the wrong wh-word (when).

lines.t: Could you keep it down a bit? I'm trying to study.

options: Sure, I'll keep it for you until Monday.
It's down the hall on the left.
Sorry about that. I'll put my headphones on.
I studied there last year.
optionNotes: Correct: apologizes and offers to be quieter.
questions.explanation: 'Keep it down' means 'be quieter'. C apologizes and solves the problem. A and B take the words literally.

lines.t: I thought you said the shuttle ran every fifteen minutes.

options: I said I'd go running with you tomorrow.
The shuttle stop is across the street.
It takes fifteen minutes to get there.
It does, but not after nine at night.
optionNotes: Gives a location; doesn't address the confusion.
Repeats 'fifteen minutes' but talks about travel time, not frequency.
Correct: confirms the information and explains the exception.
questions.explanation: The speaker is confused because the shuttle isn't coming as expected. D explains why: the schedule changes at night. This is an implied complaint that needs an explanation.

lines.t: Is the library open late tonight?

options: Yes, until midnight during exam week.
I was late for class this morning.
I returned the books yesterday.
It's the tall building by the lake.
optionNotes: Correct: answers yes and gives the closing time.
Related to libraries but doesn't answer.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question about opening hours. A answers yes and adds a useful detail.

lines.t: Which room is the study group meeting in?

options: We're meeting at around seven.
Room 3B, the one with the whiteboard.
There are about six of us in the group.
I'm studying for the biology exam.
questions.explanation: 'Which room' needs a room. Only B gives one; A and C answer different questions.

lines.t: The bookstore's out of the textbook, and class starts Monday.

options: Yes, the bookstore opens at ten on Mondays.
The class starts at nine, I think.
Have you checked whether the library has a reserve copy?
I sold all my old textbooks last spring.
optionNotes: Repeats 'bookstore' and 'Monday' but ignores the problem.
Repeats 'class starts' but adds nothing useful.
Correct: offers a solution to the problem.
Talks about the listener's own books, not the speaker's problem.
questions.explanation: The speaker states a problem without asking a question. The best reply offers help: C suggests a practical solution.

lines.t: How did your presentation go this morning?

options: It's about renewable energy.
I'm going to present it on Friday.
Professor Lee is in charge of it.
Better than I expected, actually.
optionNotes: Wrong time: the presentation already happened this morning.
questions.explanation: 'How did it go?' asks for an evaluation of a past event. D gives one. B uses the future, which contradicts 'this morning'.

lines.t: You wouldn't happen to have a spare charger, would you?

options: No, I wouldn't charge you for that.
Sorry, mine's at home. But the front desk lends them out.
My phone's battery lasts all day.
It happened just before the meeting.
optionNotes: Correct: says no politely and suggests an alternative.
Talks about the listener's phone, not the request.
questions.explanation: This is a polite, indirect request. B declines but helpfully suggests where to get one. A and D are sound-alike traps.

options: Next Thursday, by midnight.
It's about five pages.
I'll write it at the library.
Yes, I've already paid my dues.
questions.explanation: 'When' needs a time. A gives the deadline.

lines.t: I don't suppose the gym's open on public holidays.

options: I suppose I'll go on holiday in May.
Yes, I'm open to that idea.
Actually, it is. Just with shorter hours.
The gym's right next to the pool.
optionNotes: Repeats 'suppose' and 'holiday' but ignores the question.
Plays on 'open' with a different meaning.
Correct: corrects the speaker's assumption and gives a detail.
questions.explanation: 'I don't suppose...' is an indirect question: is the gym open on holidays? C answers it ('Actually, it is'), correcting the speaker's guess.
